title: How Trak works
intro: Trak does four jobs for you: scheduling, assessing, planning training and preparing for matches. It starts with setting up your season.
beforeSquad: Squad: check every player is there. Open a player to set their positions and roles.
beforePlan: Season plan: set the squad's objectives for the season, each player's objectives, and how often you evaluate.
beforeFormations: Formations: save the shapes you play, ready to use for a match.
weekIntro: From then on, Trak is four jobs.
scheduling1: Add trainings, matches and other events in Events, or with +.
scheduling2: An event stays a draft until you publish it. Then players and parents see the time, the place, the kit and your note.
scheduling3: Families can tell you a player can't make it. You see it on the event.
assessingPlayer: Assess player, from +, records how a player is doing, with a message for them. Save it as a draft, or publish it for the player and their parents to read.
assessingDue: When an evaluation is due, Home tells you. Everyone starts where they were last time, so you change only who moved.
assessingObjectives: Each player objective is Met or Not yet.
training1: Plan a session from drills, fitted to the number of players you have.
training2: On the day, Who's here is the register. Afterwards, notes keep what happened.
training3: Drills is the library: search it, keep drills in My drills, or browse the three kinds of practice.
matches1: Before a match: the logistics, then the game plan: the line-up, each player's job and your tactics. Share it with the team.
matches2: After the match: the evaluation. Add the result and a word on each player, then publish it.
goodFamilies: Players and parents see only what you publish or share. Drafts and your private notes stay with you.
goodHome: Home shows what needs you each day.
goodSettings: Settings: your language (English or Ελληνικά) and which alerts Trak sends you.
